outcomeNote: A mishna stating a tannaitic dispute; it is analysed in the gemara that follows.

segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ הָאֵבֶר וְהַבָּשָׂר הַמְדוּלְדָּלִין בְּאָדָם – טְהוֹרִים. מֵת הָאָדָם – הַבָּשָׂר טָהוֹר. הָאֵבֶר מְטַמֵּא מִשּׁוּם אֵבֶר מִן הַחַי, וְאֵינוֹ מְטַמֵּא מִשּׁוּם אֵבֶר מִן הַמֵּת, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר. וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מְטַהֵר.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» «The limb and the flesh» of a person that were partially severed and remain «hanging from a person are ritually pure,» although there is no potential for healing. If «the person died, the» hanging «flesh is ritually pure,» as its halakhic status is that of flesh severed from a living person. «The» hanging «limb imparts impurity as a limb» severed «from the living and does not impart impurity as a limb from a corpse;» this is «the statement of Rabbi Meir. And Rabbi Shimon deems» the flesh and the limb «ritually pure.»

moves.summary: hanging limb and flesh of a living person are pure, and once he dies the flesh is pure while the limb imparts impurity as a limb from the living — Rabbi Meir
moves.about: whether a limb left hanging from a person who then died imparts impurity as a limb from the living, Rabbi Meir holding that it does and Rabbi Shimon deeming it pure

moves.summary: Rabbi Shimon dissents and deems both limb and flesh pure

edges.cueHe: דברי רבי מאיר. ורבי שמעון מטהר
